subject: NovaEdge discovery — SLOs, topology & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@novaedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: NovaEdge discovery — SLOs, topology & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. High-level recap and the asks we agreed to so we have a single source of truth: 

Pain points you described
- Unpredictable tail latency on high-concurrency windows (Black Friday–like spikes during batch jobs).
- Cost is a gating factor: current self-hosted infra is expensive and brittle at >150 qps sustained.
- Data sensitivity: audit logs and retention controls required by your compliance team; preference for VPC/private control plane.

Goals / success criteria you gave
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 120 ms for typical prompts (350 tokens in, ~150 tokens out).
- Sustained throughput target for Phase 1: 200 requests/sec with headroom for 400 burst.
- Production-ready by early May (procurement/PO window mid-April).
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and ability to support customer-managed KMS.

Model & workload notes
- You plan to run two model families: a tuned open LLM for most traffic and a larger LLM ensemble for high-quality responses on sensitive flows.
- Typical prompt size ~350 tokens; generation avg ~150 tokens.
- KV cache effectiveness expected to be moderate (session-heavy).

Redwood fit & recommended path forward
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) for predictable throughput with an autoscale burst pool to handle peaks, or Private (VPC) deploy if you must keep the control plane inside your network.
- Smart routing + prefix/KV caching to reduce unit cost while meeting your latency SLO.

Action items (mutual)
1) Redwood: share a short mutual action plan and topology sketch (attached). I’ve included a baseline cost/throughput table for two deployment options.
2) NovaEdge: share 7-day sample traffic (qps by minute) and any retention/audit constraints for logs.
3) Schedule technical deep-dive with your infra and security + our Solutions Engineering (Ben) and Infra lead (Jonas). Proposed window: Fri Mar 24, 09:00 PT — please confirm.
4) Procurement: NovEdge procurement indicated target PO by Apr 15 — we’ll coordinate the SOW/contract draft once we lock the topology.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, topology-sketch.png

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll plan the deep-dive with Ben & Jonas and bring a PS/PO template for procurement.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform for low-latency, reliable LLMs.

Hi Sarah — copying a few quick technical notes ahead of Friday’s deep-dive so the meeting can focus on tradeoffs and a runbook.

Assumptions from today’s call (please correct):
- Typical prompt: 350 tokens in, 150 tokens generation.
- Target sustained qps: 200 req/s; burst to 400 req/s for short windows.

Options we’ll layout in the meeting:
1) Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool)
   - Predictable latency, reserved GPU pool (N GPUs) with an autoscale buffer.
   - Best fit if you want managed infra and clear SLOs.
   - We can provide KMS integrations and SOC2 artifacts; some network constraints remain (we’ll detail).
2) Private (VPC) deployment
   - Full private control plane on your VPC; supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and tighter audit controls.
   - Slightly longer lead time for deployment and testing.

Performance targets & capacity sketch (quick math)
- Baseline token throughput estimate: 200 qps * (350 + 150) = ~100k tokens/sec total.
- With mixed precision and KV caching we estimate ~30–45% token-level cost saving for repeated sessions.
- Suggested pilot: 2 A100-equivalent GPUs to validate latency/throughput; can scale to 4-6 for production depending on actual model footprints and quantization.

On the deep-dive agenda I’ll cover: exact model sizing, kernel/runtime tuning (sequence-length dependent), benchmark harness for your traffic samples, and fallback routing for model variants. Jonas will cover topology (multi-region fallback, ingress routing, audit log retention).

Attachments: topology-sketch.png (sketch of three options: Dedicated-only, Private-VPC, Hybrid with regional fallback).

Proposed deliverables after deep-dive:
- Deployment decision (Dedicated vs Private) and cost envelope
- Mutual action plan with milestones (prep, pilot, production)
- SOC2 artifacts & KMS integration notes for legal/procurement

See you Friday — Ben
